About this tracker

I'm a Filipino-Chinese student majoring in Industrial Engineering, with a strong passion for politics and economics. I built this dashboard to stay informed about what's happening around me — a single place to follow labor, inflation and GDP across countries, log my own views, and connect political developments to what's moving markets.

Data: World Bank · FRED (BLS/BEA) · ECB / Eurostat · Philippine Statistics Authority.  Not investment advice — a personal research log.

Macro indicators

📊 2026 GDP growth — US, EU, East Asia & ASEAN
Full-year 2026 forecasts (IMF / national agencies / street, Oct 2026). Growth clusters around AI exposure: the hardware chain (Taiwan, Singapore, Vietnam) leads, the EU core and Thailand lag.
East AsiaASEANUnited StatesEurope
Vietnam shown at 6.9% (range 6.3–7.6). Philippines: street ~4.4–5.1%, government target cut to 3.5–4.5%. Taiwan: official 11.05% after +15.4% y/y in Q1.
🛢️ SEA oil-shock exposure — who gets hurt, who gains
My ranking (stylized score, not an index): net energy trade position × Gulf supply concentration ÷ incoming growth momentum. The Philippines stacks all three the wrong way; Brunei flips the sign. Sources: ORF, Maybank, The Diplomat, IEEFA (2026).
Gulf dependence by commodity
Share of each import sourced from the Gulf. The ranking changes by commodity: crude says Philippines/Vietnam; Thailand’s exposure runs through fertilizer, Indonesia’s and Singapore’s through gas.
CountryCrude oilDieselGasN-fertilizerNotes
Philippines95%——10%~7% of crude from Malaysia as the non-Gulf fallback
Vietnam88%———second-highest crude dependence
Malaysia59%———net exporter overall; imports Gulf crude for refining
Singapore52%16%17%—natural gas = 95% of power generation
Indonesia20%8.4%37%—Gulf LPG alone = 30% of total imports
Thailand—6.8%28%67% (urea 75%)Saudi Arabia its biggest fertilizer supplier
Wrinkles: Indonesia internalizes the hit via fuel subsidies (budget + rupiah take the damage); Singapore’s refiners are paid by the same wide crack spreads that hurt consumers.
🌏 Top economies in Southeast Asia▾

Indonesia is the largest economy in Southeast Asia at over US$1.5 trillion — bigger than the next two combined. Thailand is upper middle-income and #3 in ASEAN (used to be top-2), with the Philippines close behind at #6. The bottom half of the region is tiny by comparison: Myanmar through Timor-Leste together are smaller than Singapore alone. (Smaller-economy figures approximate — double-check.)

SEA real GDP growth since 1990 (%) — hover for values · Timor-Leste excluded (±35–58% swings crush the scale)

Watch: Vietnam ($527B) is within ~7% of Thailand ($562B) and growing nearly 3× as fast — the #3 spot could change hands within a few years.
